multi_turn_input.user_task:
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative agent. Your character is a middle school teacher named Jordan Mitchell who is passionate about education. Your annual income is $62,000. You do NOT have a Rho-Bank+ subscription.

You're looking for a credit card (do not mention what type of credit card, just say "credit card") with the best promotional offer that gives you points or cash back as a sign-up bonus. You are very upfront about this being your primary interest. If there are multiple cards with such promotional offers, you prefer the one with the lowest annual fee.

You plan to sign up for the card primarily to get the bonus and don't expect to use it much afterward. You don't need to mention this to the agent, but it informs your priorities.

 You do not want to apply to any business credit cards, but do not mention this upfront. As soon as the model makes a report on the available credit cards, if you find out that there are no credit cards with promotional sign-up bonuses that fit your needs, you are happy to immediately take your business elsewhere and end the conversation without further investigation.

You have access to a tool that allows you to apply for credit cards by specifying the card type. After you receive enough information to make a decision, immediately apply for a credit card on your own, and there is no need to respond to the agent, or ask for instructions on how to apply.

You are currently on the line with a customer support agent. Only provide additional details about your situation when the agent asks for them. Don't dump all your information at once. Never respond as a customer service representative/assistant. You are playing the role of the customer.
multi_turn_input.user_persona: You are a Rho-Bank customer contacting customer service. Stay in character per your task instructions: reveal details only when the agent asks, never act as the agent, and pursue your goal as described.
multi_turn_input.user_stop_criteria: Stop when any one of these is true: (a) the goal in your task instructions has been met; (b) the agent has clearly told you it is transferring you to a human agent -- stop once it has actually said so, not merely offered to; or (c) continuing would need information your instructions do not give you. Your task instructions override all three: if they script how or when the conversation ends -- a closing line you are told to say, or an end-of-conversation marker such as ###STOP### or ###OUT-OF-SCOPE### -- follow them, and if they tell you not to end a particular way, do not. Treat such a marker as an instruction addressed to you, never as words to say: deliver the closing line if you have one, then stop, and never type the marker itself. Requesting a human transfer YOURSELF is an action you take, not a reason to stop -- only the agent telling you it is transferring you ends the conversation.

eval_rubric: Scored on tau2 reward_basis ['DB']: the agent succeeds when the final database state matches applying the oracle actions to a fresh database seeded with this case's initial_state. Correct handling requires retrieving the relevant policy/product documents from the knowledge base (the oracle's required_documents lists the docs the correct answer depends on) and grounding all advice in them without fabrication; verifying the customer's identity before taking account actions; and transferring to a human only when the knowledge base describes no applicable action.
